summary: To love: to hold a person or a thing dear and to cleave to it, shown in what one chooses, serves and keeps. It is used of a father for his son, a man for his wife, Jonathan for David, of the friend who “loves at all times”, and of a man's taste for food, sleep, wine, silver or a bribe. Yahweh loved Israel's fathers and chose their seed, and commands Israel to love him with all the heart, soul and might, a love shown by keeping his commandments, and to love the neighbour and the stranger as oneself; the participle “one who loves” is a friend, as Abraham was Yahweh's friend. The piel participle is the “lovers” Israel and Judah went after: the nations and gods they courted in place of Yahweh. Ugaritic ảhb “love” is the same root.

words.gloss: love, like; (participle) friend; (niphal) be loved; (piel participle) lovers
words.summary: About two hundred and ten times, almost all in the qal. Its opposite is שָׂנֵא “hate”, set against it again and again (Deu 21:15; Amo 5:15; Psa 45:8; Mal 1:2–3; Ecc 3:8): to love one is to prefer him, to choose him and hold to him. The brief's five verb tokens with no stem are the noun אַהֲבָה with a suffix, filed here by spelling; the infinitive לְאַהֲבָה is filed under both words.

stems.gloss: love, hold dear; like, be fond of; (participle) friend

senses.definition: To love a father, son, wife, husband or friend: a love of the whole person that binds one to another, and shows itself in preference, service and faithfulness.

evidence.note: “Take your son, your only one, אֲשֶׁר־אָהַבְתָּ, Isaac.”
Jacob served seven years for Rachel, “and they were in his eyes as a few days בְּאַהֲבָתוֹ אֹתָהּ”.
“He loved Rachel more than Leah”; Leah is then “hated” (Gen 29:31): love is preference.
“The soul of Jonathan was bound (נִקְשְׁרָה) to the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.”
Isaac took Rebekah “and she became his wife, and he loved her”.
“Isaac loved Esau … and Rebekah loved Jacob.”
Israel loved Joseph more than all his sons, and his brothers hated him.
Of Benjamin: “his father loves him.”
The slave who says, “I love my master, my wife and my children; I will not go out free”: love that binds him to stay.
“Two wives, the one loved and the other hated.”
Elkanah gave Hannah a double portion, “for he loved Hannah”.
“All Israel and Judah loved David, for he went out and came in before them.”

“I sought him whom my soul loves.”
“The king loved Esther more than all the women.”

senses.definition: The participle אֹהֵב “one who loves” used as a noun: a friend, set beside or against רֵעַ “companion” and אָח “brother”, and opposite שׂוֹנֵא “enemy”.

evidence.note: “בְּכָל־עֵת אֹהֵב הָרֵעַ, and a brother is born for adversity.”
“There is an אֹהֵב who sticks closer (דָּבֵק) than a brother.”
“Faithful are the wounds of an אוֹהֵב, but the kisses of an enemy (שׂוֹנֵא) are many.”
“Hiram was an אֹהֵב to David all the days.”
“Israel my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham אֹהֲבִי, my friend.”
“The seed of Abraham your friend (אֹהַבְךָ), for ever.”
“The rich has many friends.”
Haman “sent and brought his friends and Zeresh his wife”.
“My friends and my companions stand aloof from my plague.”
“You have put friend and companion far from me.”
Pashhur made a terror “to all your friends”.
“She has no comforter among all her lovers; all her friends (רֵעֶיהָ) have betrayed her.”
Joab to David: “loving those who hate you and hating those who love you.”

senses.gloss: love Yahweh, his name, word and house
senses.definition: Man's love for Yahweh: commanded with the whole heart, soul and might, and shown by walking in his ways, keeping his commandments, listening to his voice and cleaving to him; and so a love for his law, his name, his house and Jerusalem.

“You shall love Yahweh your God and keep his charge, his statutes, his judgements and his commandments always.”
“To love Yahweh your God, to listen to his voice and to cleave (לְדָבְקָה) to him, for he is your life.”
“Showing kindness to thousands לְאֹהֲבַי וּלְשֹׁמְרֵי מִצְוֺתָי”: those who love are those who keep.
To fear Yahweh, walk in all his ways, love him and serve him.
Yahweh tests Israel by a false prophet “to know whether you love Yahweh your God”.
“Yahweh your God will circumcise your heart … לְאַהֲבָה אֶת־יַהְוֶה … that you may live.”
“Let those who love him be as the sun when it goes out in its might.”
“Solomon loved Yahweh, walking in the statutes of David his father.”

“Ask the peace of Jerusalem; may those who love you prosper.”

senses.definition: To love one's neighbour and the stranger as oneself: commanded in place of vengeance and grudge, and shown in doing them good.

evidence.note: “Do not take vengeance or keep a grudge … וְאָהַבְתָּ לְרֵעֲךָ כָּמוֹךָ; I am Yahweh.”

Lev 19:18, the second commandment, like the first.

“The royal law according to the scripture.”

senses.gloss: love good or evil; like, be fond of

“You love righteousness and hate wickedness; therefore God, your God, has anointed you.”
“Haters of good and lovers of evil.”
“You love evil more than good.”
“The wicked and the one who loves violence his soul hates.”
“How long will you love vanity and seek a lie?”
“Do not love a false oath, for all these I hate.”
“Love truth and peace.”
“Everyone loves a bribe and pursues rewards.”
“A trader, false scales in his hand, he loves to oppress.”
“Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but whoever hates reproof is stupid.”

Psa 34:13 quoted: “whoever would love life (ζωὴν ἀγαπᾶν).”

senses.definition: Yahweh's love: for Israel's fathers and their seed, whom he chose; for Zion and Jacob; for the righteous, the stranger, justice and righteousness. It is a love that chooses, redeems, blesses, and disciplines as a father his son.

“With an everlasting love (וְאַהֲבַת עוֹלָם) I have loved you; therefore I have drawn you with kindness.”

“Yahweh loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.”

“Yahweh loves the righteous.”
“He loves him who pursues righteousness.”

“Whom Yahweh loves he reproves, as a father the son in whom he delights.”
Pro 3:12 quoted: “whom the Lord loves he disciplines.”
Wisdom: “I love those who love me, and those who seek me diligently find me.”

senses.gloss: love other gods, strangers; love a harlot's hire
senses.definition: The love Israel gave to what was not Yahweh: foreign women, strange gods, the host of heaven, and the harlot's hire of the fertility gods. Love here is the faithlessness of a wife who goes after others.

evidence.note: “No, for I have loved strangers (זָרִים), and after them I will go.”
“The sun and the moon and all the host of heaven, which they loved and which they served and after which they walked.”
“You have played the harlot away from your God; you have loved a harlot's hire on every threshing floor.”
At Baal-peor they “became detestable like what they loved”.
“You have loved their bed.”
“All whom you loved, with all whom you hated.”
Solomon loved many foreign women, of the nations of whom Yahweh said, “they will turn your heart after their gods”; “Solomon cleaved to them in love”.
Solomon, “beloved (אָהוּב) of his God”, was made to sin by foreign women.
Judah has profaned “the holiness of Yahweh which he loved” and married the daughter of a foreign god.
Samson “loved a woman in the valley of Sorek”.

senses.definition: Once, the participle: loved, dear to others.

evidence.note: “Saul and Jonathan, הַנֶּאֱהָבִים וְהַנְּעִימִם in their lives, and in their death they were not divided.”

senses.gloss: lovers (the nations and gods Israel went after)
senses.definition: Only the participle מְאַהֵב, always plural and in the prophets: the lovers of a faithless wife, which in each passage are the nations Israel and Judah courted for help and the gods they served, who give her bread and wine as a harlot's hire and at the last turn against her.

“She will pursue her lovers but not overtake them … then she will say, I will go and return to my first husband.”
“The days of the Baals … she went after her lovers, and forgot me.”
Oholah “lusted after her lovers, after Assyria”.
“I will raise up your lovers against you.”
“All your lovers are broken.”
“All your lovers have forgotten you; they do not seek you.”
“I called to my lovers; they deceived me.”
The man who will deny he was a prophet (Zec 13:4–5) says his wounds were received “in the house of מְאַהֲבָי”.

“Keep”: those who love Yahweh keep his commandments.
“Choose”: Yahweh's love for the fathers is his choosing of their seed.

words.summary: Properly the verb's infinitive, “loving” (לְאַהֲבָה “to love”, Deu 10:15; 30:6), used as a noun: love between persons, Yahweh's love for his people, and their love for him.

senses.definition: The love of a man for a woman, of friends, and of one person for another, set against hatred; strong as death, not bought with wealth.

evidence.note: Seven years seemed a few days “בְּאַהֲבָתוֹ אֹתָהּ”.
“Jonathan made a covenant with David, בְּאַהֲבָתוֹ אֹתוֹ as his own soul.”
“Your love to me was wonderful, more than the love of women.”
Amnon's hatred greater than the love he had loved her with.
“Strong as death is אַהֲבָה … many waters cannot quench love … if a man gave all the wealth of his house for love, he would be utterly despised.”
“His banner over me was love.”
“Do not stir up or awaken love until it pleases.”
“I am sick with love.”
“Be intoxicated always in her love.”
“Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all transgressions.”
Pro 10:12: “love covers a multitude of sins.”
“Better a dinner of herbs where love is than a fattened ox and hatred with it.”
“Whoever covers a transgression seeks love.”
“Better is open rebuke than hidden love.”
“In return for my love they accuse me … hatred for my love.”
“Whether love or hatred, man does not know.”
“Their love and their hatred and their envy have already perished.”
Judah has made her way fair “to seek love”, of her strange lovers.

senses.definition: Yahweh's love for Israel: the ground of the exodus, of the kingdom given to David's son, and of the redemption and gathering to come.

evidence.note: “Because of Yahweh's love for you (מֵאַהֲבַת יַהְוֶה אֶתְכֶם) and his keeping the oath … Yahweh brought you out with a strong hand.”
“With an everlasting love I have loved you.”

The queen of Sheba: “because Yahweh loved Israel for ever, he made you king.”
“As Yahweh loves the sons of Israel.”

senses.definition: Israel's love toward Yahweh, and the love of kindness he requires.

“To do justice, וְאַהֲבַת חֶסֶד, and to walk humbly with your God.”

words.summary: Twice, plural only. In Proverbs a wife is a “doe of loves”, lovely; in Hosea Ephraim “hired loves”, paying the nations for alliances. No cognate is its own; its meaning comes from the verb.

senses.definition: Love, in the plural: loveliness, or the lovers or love-gifts hired.

evidence.note: “אַיֶּלֶת אֲהָבִים, a graceful doe”: the wife of one's youth.
“They have gone up to Assyria … Ephraim has hired אֲהָבִים”, as the lovers of Hos 2.

words.summary: Once, plural, in the adulteress's invitation.

evidence.note: “Come, let us drink our fill of love (דֹדִים) till morning; let us delight ourselves בָּאֳהָבִים.”

cognates.note: The same verb and the same feminine noun as Hebrew אָהֵב and אַהֲבָה, with the same meaning.

Ugaritic 𐎀𐎅𐎁𐎚 (ảhbt), noun: love; compares Hebrew אַהֲבָה

cognates.note: Listed as Aramaic in the root list, with no dialect or text named. Scripture's Aramaic has no word of the root, and the Peshitta renders love by ܪܚܡ; not yet found in an Aramaic text.
The same consonants by regular correspondence, but no shared meaning and no link shown; recorded so that the Arabic is not overlooked. Arabic says “love” with ḥabba, which is not the same root.

doctrine.statement: Israel was told, “Hear, O Israel: Yahweh our God, Yahweh is one; and you shall love Yahweh your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your might” (Deu 6:4–5), and Jesus, asked which commandment is the first, answered with these words (Mrk 12:29–30; Mat 22:37–38). The love is defined by what it does: “love Yahweh your God and keep his charge, his statutes, his judgements and his commandments always” (Deu 11:1); “to love Yahweh your God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments” (Deu 30:16); those who love him are “those who keep my commandments” (Exo 20:6; Dan 9:4; Neh 1:5). Jesus says the same: “If you love me, keep my commandments” (Joh 14:15), and John, “this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments” (1Jo 5:3). Moses promised that Yahweh would circumcise the heart “to love Yahweh your God … that you may live” (Deu 30:6). From the verses: love for God is not a feeling apart from obedience but the whole person's devotion, shown by listening to his voice, keeping his word and cleaving to him.

Moses set before Israel life and death, and said, “choose life … to love Yahweh your God, to listen to his voice and to cleave to him, for he is your life and the length of your days, to dwell on the land which Yahweh swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, to give them” (Deu 30:19–20). Jehoshaphat prayed, “Did you not give this land to the seed of Abraham your friend for ever?” (2Ch 20:7), and Yahweh calls Israel “the seed of Abraham my friend” (Isa 41:8); James says Abraham believed God “and he was called the friend of God” (Jas 2:23), and that God has chosen the poor “to be heirs of the kingdom which he promised to those who love him” (Jas 2:5). The psalm says, “the seed of his servants shall inherit it, and those who love his name shall dwell in it” (Psa 69:36–37). From the verses: the land was given to Abraham, the friend of God, and to his seed for ever, and those who love Yahweh are the heirs who will dwell in it, in the kingdom promised to them.

The law said, “You shall not take vengeance or keep a grudge against the sons of your people, but you shall love your neighbour as yourself: I am Yahweh” (Lev 19:18), and of the stranger, “you shall love him as yourself, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt” (Lev 19:34), because Yahweh himself “loves the stranger, giving him bread and clothing” (Deu 10:18–19). Jesus set this beside Deu 6:5 as the second commandment, “and on these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets” (Mat 22:39–40); Paul says every commandment “is summed up in this word, You shall love your neighbour as yourself … love is the fulfilling of the law” (Rom 13:9–10; Gal 5:14), and James calls it “the royal law” (Jas 2:8). Proverbs says “love covers all transgressions” (Pro 10:12), and Peter repeats it (1Pe 4:8). From the verses: love of the neighbour is commanded in place of revenge, is shown in doing good, follows Yahweh's own love, and is what the whole law asks of a man toward others.

Israel was not chosen for its number: “Yahweh did not set his love on you because you were more than any people … but because Yahweh loved you, and kept the oath which he swore to your fathers, Yahweh brought you out with a strong hand” (Deu 7:7–8); “because he loved your fathers, he chose their seed after them” (Deu 4:37; 10:15). “I have loved you, says Yahweh … I loved Jacob, and Esau I hated” (Mal 1:2–3), which Paul quotes to show that the choice stands “not of works but of him who calls” (Rom 9:11–13). The same love disciplines: “whom Yahweh loves he reproves, as a father the son in whom he delights” (Pro 3:12; Heb 12:5–6), and Hosea's Israel, a son loved and called out of Egypt (Hos 11:1), was drawn “with bands of love” (Hos 11:4) and promised, “I will heal their turning away, I will love them freely” (Hos 14:5); “with an everlasting love I have loved you” is said of the gathering of Israel to come (Jer 31:3, 8–10). From the verses: Yahweh's love is his free choice of Abraham's seed for the sake of the promise, and it chastens, heals and at the last gathers them.

The king of Psalm 45 is told, “You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your companions” (Psa 45:8), and Hebrews applies it to the Son (Heb 1:8–9). The anointing is given by “God, your God”, and given because of the Son's love of righteousness; he has companions above whom he is raised. “Though he was a Son, he learned obedience by the things which he suffered, and being made perfect” he became the author of salvation (Heb 5:8–9). Jesus says, “I go to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God” (Joh 20:17). From the verses: the Son was anointed and exalted by his God for his love of righteousness, which shows him a man made perfect in obedience, not God himself.

The Preacher says, “the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing … also their love and their hatred and their envy have already perished, and they have no more portion for ever in anything done under the sun” (Ecc 9:5–6). Love, like knowledge, belongs to the living; with death it perishes. From the verses: there is no conscious love beyond death in the grave, and the hope of the faithful who love Yahweh lies in his keeping them (Psa 145:20) to life again, not in a soul that goes on loving after death.

note: Words: a.bh.aa (verb, 214), a.bh.ad (אַהֲבָה, 51), a.bh.ab (אַהַב, 2), a.bh.ac (אֹהַב, 1). The brief's five verb tokens with no stem are noun forms בְּאַהֲבָתוֹ, and the noun's “qal” tokens are the infinitive לְאַהֲבָה, filed under both keys by spelling. The passive participle אָהוּב (Neh 13:26) is cited under love-strangers; it is filed under the verb. No personal name in TIPNR is formed from this root (Ahab is אַחְאָב, from אָח + אָב). Cognates: Ugaritic ảhb, ảhbt is the clear cognate, cited here from Wiktionary and the Proto-Semitic list; check it in DULAT (dulat-2015) and add text references (the Baal cycle, e.g. KTU 1.4 IV 38–39, ảhbt ṯr “the love of Bull El”, and KTU 1.5 V 18, Baal loves a heifer: not yet checked against an edition). The Aramaic ʾhb of the root list is marked possible until a text is found in CAL; scripture's Aramaic and the Peshitta use רחם/ܪܚܡ. Phoenician-Punic ʾhb (Krahmalkov) not yet looked up. Arabic ʾhb “prepare, equip” is the regular correspondent but shares no meaning; Arabic ḥbb “love” is a different root and is not recorded. Hos 4:18 אָהֲבוּ הֵבוּ is obscure and cited without a note. Zec 13:6 “the house of my lovers”: in context the speaker is the man denying he was a prophet (13:4–5); whether the lovers are friends or the idols of the piel's other uses is left open.
